title: Điện thoại của tôi bị ướt
pronunciation: Dien thoai cua toi bi uot

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Điện thoại của tôi bị ướt names the problem so staff or a helpful local can act on it. Use it when My phone got wet is the clearest way to explain what changed, went missing, or needs attention.

sections.title: Quick say
sections.body: Say Điện thoại của tôi bị ướt calmly and show the proof if you have it: phone screen, charger, SIM card, Wi-Fi screen, or outlet. After that, let the other person ask one follow-up or point you to the right next step.

sections.body: Read the cards left to right: first catch the request shape, then the place, item, action, or time detail, and finally the complete phrase.

sections.title: Useful nearby phrases
sections.body: Use these nearby pages when the conversation shifts from My phone got wet to another phone, internet, or power need.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Use this as soon as the problem is clear enough to name. It is especially useful at a counter or desk where someone can look at the photo, receipt, bag, booking, or phone screen with you.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: Keep the explanation simple and show the evidence if you can. A short phrase plus a photo, receipt, or booking usually works better than adding more English.

sections.title: Explore next
